method: Direct Thumb big-endian disassembly of handlers and named backend paths. SDIO virtual dispatch resolved against module tables and the initialized ROM object. UART/framework and general OS helpers are not formally proven transitively.

sdio_binding.consumer: ultra_spectra binding index 1 stores its SDIO interface at 0x20defe38; module table 0xa0622bfc identifies interface SUID 0x1216c.
sdio_binding.provider: sdio module request table 0xa06058ec uses the same SUID. Interface getter 0xa03c07b6 returns [0x208584c0] = 0xa0605968; that ROM object points to vtable 0xa060596c.
sdio_binding.runtime_limit: Binding is resolved from this image; a physical run must still establish that the live module is initialized. Each handler checks A045EA8C before accessing this interface.

queries.name: ultra_spectra.get_sdio_counters
queries.purpose: Read the WiFi SDIO command, transfer, timeout and error counters without clearing them.
queries.review_evidence: A0454F76 checks card availability, calls vtable +0x14 with port 0 and a 40-byte stack buffer, and prints only on interface result 1. Resolved A03C0882 -> A03C67C0 -> A03C129A copies ten words from driver object +0x3c4 into that buffer; no counter reset or card transaction.
queries.side_effects_assessment: Cached RAM reads, stack writes and UART output. Counters remain untouched by the getter.

queries.name: ultra_spectra.get_sdio_caps
queries.purpose: Read the SDIO manufacturer/device IDs, function capabilities, block sizes, and speed support needed by the emulator.
queries.review_evidence: A0454796 sends request 0x65 into a 0xac-byte stack structure, then request 0x64 into the same request output. Resolved A03C668E queues to A03C69C4; 0x65 selects A03C6D14, which copies cached CCCR/FBR and manufacturer/device fields via A03C130E/A03C1322/A03C12D6; 0x64 selects A03C6A66, which copies cached function count and function sizes via A03C138E/A03C13A0/A03C13A4. Formatting runs only after successful request completion.
queries.side_effects_assessment: Two serialized driver requests, semaphore/queue bookkeeping, cached RAM reads, caller-buffer writes and UART output. These selectors do not issue discovery, configuration, radio connection, reset or nonvolatile writes.
queries.result_limitations: The helper waits for request completion internally; host timeout is a capture bound, not a guarantee that every firmware fault is bounded. These fields are cached capability values, not a new card enumeration.

queries.name: ultra_spectra.get_sdio_status
queries.purpose: Read and dump the current 32 bytes at SDIO function 0 offsets 0x00..0x1f.
queries.review_evidence: A04546C4 -> resolved vtable +0x20 A03C08A2 -> A03C6816 -> A03C4BD8. Last helper invokes A03C506C with direction 0, function 0, address 0, length 0x20 and a stack output buffer. A03C52E4 loops over exactly 32 bytes using A03C13DC. A045EE36 prints the successful read as hex.
queries.side_effects_assessment: 32 SDIO read transactions and normal controller/request bookkeeping; this will increment the SDIO counters. No write request to card configuration, connection, scan, or persistent settings is selected.

code_evidence.description: CMD52 bit 31 is set only when direction equals 1; supplied direction 0 leaves write bit clear and stores response byte in caller output

queries.result_limitations: CCCR registers are live, so compare to the cached capability dump without assuming atomicity. Handler success alone is weak: A03C6816 returns 1 after its helper even if that helper prints a read failure; require the 32-byte dump.

queries.name: ultra_spectra.get_iovar
queries.purpose: Read the WiFi driver integer variable mpc.
queries.review_evidence: A0453F3A consumes one bounded string (100-byte input buffer). A0459322 checks the driver pointer, calls A0459414 with no input payload and 4-byte output, and prints only on success. A0459414 passes ioctl 0x106 through getter A0459568 (vtable +0x0c), while setters use 0x107 through A045955C. The selected variable names occur in this firmware: mpc at A04585B8, nmode at A062303C. The corresponding getter output is interpreted as a little-endian 32-bit integer by A0459656.
queries.side_effects_assessment: A driver GET_VAR request with a variable name only, stack buffers, transaction bookkeeping and UART output. No setter payload or nonvolatile configuration path is selected.

code_evidence.description: bounded string argument and successful-only output

queries.result_limitations: The radio firmware can reject unsupported variables. An empty result with a normal prompt is not a successful value read. Do not use this integer handler for strings such as ver or for secret material.

queries.name: ultra_spectra.test_endian
queries.purpose: Record the compiled 16/32/64-bit endian conversion test vectors for emulator comparison.
queries.review_evidence: A045520A..A045527E prints twelve literal vectors through A0453EEE and returns; all values are fixed immediates/literals (0x0102, 0x01020304, 0x0102030405060708 and their reversed-byte counterparts). There is no hardware access.
queries.side_effects_assessment: UART output and stack/formatting bookkeeping only.
queries.result_limitations: These are compiled fixed-vector outputs. They are not evidence that the physical SDIO bus exercised all endian cases.

queries.name: webfwupdate.get_base_md
queries.purpose: Read the 16-byte base firmware digest and any matching base_md entry in local secure configuration.
queries.review_evidence: A0470EEA reads 16 bytes from the existing base-MD pointer at 20E09780 and formats 32 hex characters via A046ED8A. It then requests section web_product_update/key base_md with a 65-byte output buffer through A03C8882/A03C8696. The secure-configuration helper seeks and reads existing cached file descriptors; it never selects a file write. Missing entry is skipped because caller passed a NULL default.
queries.side_effects_assessment: Local metadata reads and UART output. Secure-config lookup uses its mutex and changes file positions; on bad/stale file reads it can close those cached handles and compact the in-memory descriptor list. No firmware update, download, or nonvolatile write.

code_evidence.description: bounded read, copy and cached-handle cleanup

queries.result_limitations: The base digest pointer is initialized by the firmware lifecycle; unlike the formatted optional configuration entry it is not null-checked by this handler. Established running firmware is the precondition. This command does not recompute the digest.

held_for_further_review.reason: Read-only ioctl 0x3f is selected, but A0458240 dereferences the WLC driver without a null check and ignores driver return status before converting uninitialized output. A live successful GET_VAR is a useful prerequisite, but the antenna value still needs an error check outside this handler. Not in this batch.
Required numeric adaptor selector is real, but absent hardware can return before setting the stack output flag; this WiFi/USB printer is not a useful target for the unguarded wired formatter.

Prior cache-refresh hold strengthened: A02DDA8A clears/rebuilds manufacturing cache AND normalizes an NVM enum via setter vtable +0x0c at A02DDB34 when its value exceeds 2. These names are not passive read-only getters.
A02E0140 leaves output length r4 uninitialized if enum is outside 1..4, including 0. Live enum precondition remains unproved.
Actual scans/discovery; not necessary to obtain the SDIO diagnostics in this batch. No claim these are intrinsically forbidden.
USB behavior/configuration mutations. Available passive USB configuration queries already captured; no newly proved useful passive USB command remains in this reviewed set.

prior_hold_correction: Manufacturing network getters may also normalize an out-of-range NVM field; earlier description as only a RAM cache refresh was incomplete.
